coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED (three, all contemporaneous with the 2022 season):

1. UGA-ARCHIVE = https://web.archive.org/web/20220803072223/https://georgiadogs.com/sports/football/coaches — Georgia's official football coaches + "Football Support Staff" directory as archived Aug. 3, 2022 (start of the 2022 season). This is the backbone of the dataset: it lists 65 people in an HTML table with a name cell and a title cell. IMPORTANT FOR QUOTE MATCHING: because name and title sit in separate table cells, the verbatim quote I supply for these rows is the TITLE CELL STRING ONLY (e.g. "Quality Control - Offense"). The person's name is in the adjacent cell of the same row and will not string-match contiguously with the title. Each such row's `note` names the person whose row the title belongs to. Where a generic title (e.g. "Quality Control - Offense", "Assistant Strength & Conditioning Coach") is shared by several people, I added a second source with a name-bearing quote wherever one existed.

2. MEDIA-GUIDE = https://archive.org/download/georgia-football-2022-media-guide/Georgia%20Football%2C%202022%20Media%20Guide_djvu.txt — the OCR full text of the official 2022 Georgia Football Media Guide (published Aug. 2022). This is a fetchable plain-text file, so quotes from it do string-match. Caveat: it is OCR of a two-column PDF staff directory, so names and titles are OCR'd into SEPARATE runs of lines. A few line groups did survive as contiguous prose and those are high-confidence (the "Quality Control", "Graduate Assistants" and "Student Assistants" lines). Everything else from this guide is a name-only quote with the title recovered by column-order alignment — flagged individually in `note`.

3. WIKIPEDIA = https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Georgia_Bulldogs_football_team — used only as a corroborating second source, and only for list items whose rendered text is contiguous with ordinary spaces. NOTE: several Wikipedia support-staff lines contain a non-breaking space (U+00A0) immediately after the en dash; I deliberately did NOT quote those, because a normalizing fetch would break the match. Wikipedia's own citation for that section points at the 2021 media guide, which is why I treated it as secondary throughout.

PEOPLE I DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED (documented reasoning, not omission by oversight):
- Matt Luke — appears in the Aug. 3, 2022 archived georgiadogs directory with the vague title "Football Staff", but he RESIGNED from Georgia on Feb. 21, 2022, before the 2022 season, and he is absent from the 2022 media guide entirely (grep count: 0). His directory card is a stale leftover. Not a 2022-season staffer; excluded.
- Eric Black, Meaghan Turcotte, Garrett Murphy, Rashawn Scott — listed in Wikipedia's support-staff/graduate-assistant lists, but ALL FOUR are absent from both the Aug. 2022 archived official directory and the 2022 media guide (grep count: 0 in the media guide for each). Wikipedia's section is sourced to the 2021 media guide, so these are almost certainly 2021 holdovers. Excluded rather than padded in. If the ring rule is generous, these four are the first candidates to re-check against a 2021 roster.

CONFIDENCE TIERS WITHIN THE DATA:
- HIGH (65 people): everyone drawn from the UGA-ARCHIVE table, plus the QC/GA/student-assistant names from the contiguous media-guide lines. Name-to-title pairing is directly attested.
- MEDIUM (Chris Blaszka, Brittany deCamp, James Ellis, Brayson Farmer, Jack Fiscella, Roderick Hall, Adam Hartwig): media-guide-only, title recovered by column-order alignment. I validated this alignment method on the same block: 13 of 13 people in that block who ALSO appear in the UGA-ARCHIVE directory matched their aligned title exactly, so the method is well-tested for this block.
- LOWER (Roger Velasquez, Drew Willson, Ben Schmidt, Ryan Madaleno): media-guide-only, and drawn from a third block where the OCR column ordering is demonstrably misaligned (alphabetical name order does not track the title order). Their titles are best-fit inferences from the remaining unassigned titles and are flagged as such in each `note`. Ryan Madaleno is independently corroborated as a trainer by a bio line ("Trainer Ryan Madaleno in May of 2021").

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT:
- NO SNAPSHOT NEAR THE TITLE GAME. The championship was Jan. 9, 2023, but the only Wayback capture of the georgiadogs football staff directory I could retrieve is Aug. 3, 2022 — a request for a Jan. 5, 2023 capture redirected back to the same Aug. 3, 2022 snapshot, and the Wayback CDX index returned 503/504 on every retry. So this roster reflects the START of the 2022 season, not the championship game itself. Any support-staff arrivals or departures between September 2022 and January 2023 are therefore NOT captured, and I have flagged no `midseason_note` for anyone because I had no source that could establish one. This is the single largest gap in the dataset.
- Scott Cochran: I specifically checked the widely-remembered Cochran leave of absence and confirmed it was AUGUST 2021, not 2022. He served three seasons as Georgia's special teams coordinator and was on staff through both the 2021 and 2022 titles (he resigned in Feb. 2024). So no midseason_note applies to him for 2022.
- One person is unnamed: the 2022 media guide's support-staff title column includes an "Equipment Intern" whose corresponding name was lost in the OCR column break. That person is real and documented by title but cannot be named, so no row exists for them.
- Roles are as-worded by the source and sometimes conflict between sources for the same person (e.g. Neyland Raper is "Director of Football Operations" in the Aug. 2022 directory but "Assistant director of football operations & recruiting" on Wikipedia's 2021-sourced list; Angela Kirkpatrick and Logen Reed likewise differ). I used the 2022 directory wording as authoritative and did not cite the conflicting Wikipedia line for those people.
- Nutrition staff (Collier Madaleno, Cate Herrmans) and the performance-chef/culinary staff are categorized "other" rather than "medical"; that is a judgment call, not a sourcing limitation.
- Jacob Russell is "Quality Control - Offense" in the Aug. 2022 directory but does not appear in the media guide's QC list (which names Bobo, Faulkner, Gordon, Sutherland, Van Gorder, Blake Lane, Pryce Tracy). Both sources are from Aug. 2022; I kept him on the directory's authority and categorized him qc. Wikipedia separately calls him an offensive graduate assistant.
- Name spelling note: the media guide renders "Montgomery Van Gorder" (two words) while the official directory renders "Montgomery VanGorder" (one word). I used the directory spelling.
